# claude_tool

[← Command index](README.md)

Run every file in a directory through Claude with a prompt template.

## Synopsis

```
claude_tool [options]
```

## Description

Walks the input directory, fills the prompt template with each file's content, sends
it to the Anthropic API, and writes the reply to the same relative path under the
output directory, so the output mirrors the input tree. Files are sent one at a time.
It suits bulk rewrites such as cleaning up decompiled code, generating documentation,
or converting formats.

The prompt file is plain text or markdown. These placeholders are replaced for each
file: `{file_content}` (the whole file), `{filename}` (e.g. `main.cpp`),
`{file_basename}` (`main`), `{file_extension}` (`.cpp`), `{input_file}` (full path),
`{input_dir}` and `{output_dir}` (the directories given with `-i` and `-o`).

The API key is read from `[UserData.Anthropic] anthropic_api_key` in `~/JoyBox.ini`.
A file that fails is counted as an error and processing moves on; the run ends with a
count of successes, skips and errors.

## Options

### Input/Output

| Option | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| `-i, --input_path <input_path>` | Directory of files to process; it must exist. |
| `-o, --output_path <output_path>` | Directory to write the replies into, mirroring the input tree; created if missing. |
| `-f, --prompt_file <prompt_file>` | Prompt template file (text or markdown) with `{file_content}` and other placeholders; required. |

### Behavior

| Option | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| `-m, --model <model>` | Anthropic model id to send requests to. Default: `claude-sonnet-4-20250514`. |
| `-w, --extensions <extensions>` | Comma-separated file extensions to process, e.g. `.cpp,.h` (the dot is optional); every file when omitted. |
| `-t, --max_tokens <max_tokens>` | Maximum number of tokens in each reply. Default: `8192`. |
| `-e, --skip_existing` | Skip input files whose output file already exists, to resume an interrupted run. |

### Common options

| Option | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| `-v, --verbose` | Enable verbose mode. |
| `-p, --pretend_run` | Do a pretend run with no permanent changes. |
| `-x, --exit_on_failure` | Enable exit on failure mode. |
| `--no-preview` | Skip the preview confirmation prompt. |

## Examples

### Process every file in a directory

```bash
claude_tool -i ./input -o ./output -f prompt.md
```

### Clean up Ghidra C++ output only

```bash
claude_tool -i ./src -o ./cleaned -f ghidra_cleanup.md -w ".cpp,.h,.c"
```

### Use a specific model with a longer reply limit

```bash
claude_tool -i ./input -o ./output -f prompt.md -m claude-sonnet-4-20250514 -t 16384
```

### Resume an interrupted run, skipping files already written

```bash
claude_tool -i ./input -o ./output -f prompt.md -e
```

### List what would be processed without calling the API

```bash
claude_tool -i ./input -o ./output -f prompt.md -p -v
```

## Notes

- API usage is billed per token; check the file count in the preview before confirming.
- Replies are written as-is, so ask the prompt for output without explanations or markdown fences if the result should be a source file.
- Large files may need a higher `--max_tokens`, or the reply is cut off.
- The `anthropic` Python package must be installed; the bootstrap's Python packages include it.
- A dry run does not need an API key.
